notes: Lines of the tờ lịch: public-domain Vietnamese folk sayings (tục ngữ, ca dao, thành ngữ: anonymous oral tradition, no author; the card names the genre, D48) and, since v0.14.1, lines of poetry (thơ) and quotations (danh ngôn) by named public-domain authors (the card names the author). Line of the day (tờ lịch): items[jd mod items.length], jd = Julian day number of the solar date shown (jdFromDate). All platforms use the same rule, so they show the same line; the line of a date may change between spec releases (v0.14.1 added the thơ / danh ngôn items between the folk ones, so every date's line changed): ports never store an index or a date → line map across spec versions.

Order: the thơ / danh ngôn items are spread evenly between the folk items (never two authored items side by side, never two neighbours by the same author), so consecutive days alternate genres; a batch that adds items re-spreads them the same way (test: spec-data.test.ts).

`complete: true` marks an item of 6 or 8 syllables that was checked to be a whole saying (or a whole line of verse that stands on its own), not one line of a lục bát couplet (6 + 8 syllables); every other 6- or 8-syllable item is rejected by the test, and so are the known halves it lists. A 14-syllable item of verse (folk or thơ) is a couplet split 6 + 8 or 7 + 7 at its first comma (or ? or ;). Ports ignore the key.

Attribution (D48): the tờ lịch shows, under the line, its genre or author like a paper calendar ("— Tục ngữ", "— Nguyễn Du"; docs/components.md Tờ lịch card). `sourceLabels` maps every allowed `source` to the strings key of its label (spec/strings/vi.json toLich.proverb.source.*; danh ngôn and thơ: the pattern {author}, so a poem shows "— Nguyễn Du", not "— Thơ Nguyễn Du"); ports render it with toLich.proverb.attribution and read it with toLich.proverb.a11y. A `source` missing from `sourceLabels` (a newer list in an older app) shows the line without an attribution, never the raw value. Adding a source value or an optional key is not a format change; ports decode `text` and `source` (and `author`) and ignore other keys.

Thơ and danh ngôn, rules for every item (test: spec-data.test.ts): `source: "thơ"` (a line or a couplet of a poem, verses joined by a comma, second verse lower-case) or `source: "danh ngôn"` (a saying or a sentence of prose); `author` = the person's common Vietnamese name as readers know it ("Nguyễn Trãi", "Khổng Tử", "Lev Tolstoy"): Vietnamese alphabet only, no honorific or title (not "Chủ tịch …", "Bác …"; a pen name that is the name readers know, "Bà Huyện Thanh Quan", is allowed by name), no dates, work or page; `authorDeathYear` = the year the author died (an integer, negative = BCE; for an uncertain date the latest plausible year, said in a note) and ≤ 1975; `sources` = at least one `{ title, note?, url? }` saying where the wording and the author were checked: a reliable published source (the author's collected works, a scholarly edition or anthology, a school textbook, an official archive, a primary-text library such as ctext.org, Wikisource or Project Gutenberg), never a quotation website or social media. `authorDeathYear` and `sources` are provenance only: no platform shows them (D22: no book titles, pages or links on any screen) and ports ignore them. Folk items carry none of `author`, `authorDeathYear`, `sources`.

Copyright (Vietnam, Luật Sở hữu trí tuệ 2005, amended 2009/2019/2022): economic rights last the author's life + 50 years and end at 24:00 on 31 December of the 50th year after the death (Điều 27 khoản 2 điểm b: life + 50; khoản 3: the term ends on 31 December), so an author who died in or before 1975 is public domain in 2026; the list does NOT rely on the quotation exception (Điều 25: quoting to comment or illustrate in one's own work), which does not fit a daily line. A translation is itself a protected derivative work (translator's life + 50): a line written in Hán, Nôm-era Hán, or a foreign language is shown either in a published Vietnamese translation whose translator also died in or before 1975 (named in `sources`, e.g. Ngô Tất Tố, Tản Đà) or in a fresh translation by the editors (note "Bản dịch: Ban biên soạn" + the original text), never in a modern Vietnamese translation still in copyright; the card still names only the author. No living or post-1975 author, no song lyrics, no misattributed or disputed quote (check Wikiquote's misattributed / disputed sections and Quote Investigator; a line that cannot be traced to the author's own text is not added, however popular), no line used against its sense in context. Tone: positive or neutral everyday wisdom; no political slogan, religious preaching, fortune or superstition (D26/D50), nothing sad, fearful, erotic or about drinking or war.

Length: a folk item ≤ 60 characters; a thơ / danh ngôn item ≤ 70 characters (a couplet of verse is longer than a proverb). Every item takes 1 or 2 lines of type.quote on the narrowest card (295 pt content width) and an authored item still 2 lines at 285 pt (a 10-pt margin for the platforms' line breakers); every attribution one line (packages/tokens-build/test/sheet-height.test.mjs).
